description: Reference to video with audio through Pika H3 Flex, Pika's adapter over MiniMax-H3. The 'ref2va' workflow takes a references list of Pika's own reference types - PikaH3FlexImageReference (up to 9), PikaH3FlexVideoReference (up to 3, motion or performance) and PikaH3FlexAudioReference - which the prompt addresses as @Image1, @Video1, @Audio1; here 'subject' (@Image1) fixes the subject and 'voice' (@Audio1) their voice; 'subject_2' and 'subject_3' are @Image2 and @Image3 when set (a null one is dropped), and a references-list variable is the way past three. An image reference is encoded at the tier's reference short edge (1024 below 768p, 2048 at 768p). Runs on the reference partition ('transformer_ref') with Pika's ref2va adapter. Pika H3 Flex is an adapter over MiniMax-H3's own weights: the five weight components (transformer, transformer_ref, text_encoder, vae, audio_vae) are loaded from MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3, pinned at the commit the H3 templates load (0919fb68, the same tensors as the 42ed227e base Pika's adapter manifest names, sampled), so they share H3's int8 cache; only the scheduler, tokenizer and processor come from Pika's repo. The adapter's sampler is fixed: its blocks run the 7-point denoising_step_list [1000, 750, 500, 250, 100, 40, 0] (6 transformer passes) on their own shift, so the template sets no num_inference_steps and no scheduler shift - stated in configuration.configs only so validate counts the passes. Seeds are not comparable with the H3 templates: the same seed on the same prompt gives a different clip, so an A/B against H3 compares samples, not a matched pair. The base match itself is sampled (Pika's own runs against the pinned base, not a bit-exact reproduction). 'resolution' picks a 16:9 bucket - 480p is 832x480, 768p is 1344x768; other ratios of the same tiers (multiples of 32): 9:16 480x832 / 768x1344, 1:1 480x480 / 768x768, 4:3 640x480 / 1024x768, 3:4 480x640 / 768x1024, 21:9 960x416 / 1536x672 - pass width and height for one. The weights load at int8 SDNQ (host_ram_gb 69). At 768p, three image references plus the voice do not fit a 24 GB card (validate refuses it): use 480p for three images, or drop one.
summary: Pika H3 Flex video with audio keeping an image's subject and an audio clip's voice.

vram_estimate.reason: Ref2VA holds every reference's encoding resident beside the video latents, so the ceiling is a fixed base, a per-voxel term for the VAE decode's conv3d activation (width * height * num_frames), and a per-reference term counted once per set slot, the voice included. gb_per_reference is classified on this template itself (lem, RTX 3090 24 GB, Pika H3 Flex at int8, 1344x768x124, 2026-11): job 791261748196 (two images + the voice, 3 references) ran with 22.0 GiB reserved at decode, projected 23.02 GB; job cdc890a03e60 (three images + the voice, 4 references) OOM'd before denoise step 1 with 19.45 GB in use and a 6.72 GiB allocation refused, at least 26.17 GB, projected 24.22 GB and refused (#1343). The refused allocation is a lower bound, not a peak, so this is a classification, not a fitted curve. base_gb and bytes_per_voxel are unchanged from the H3 calibration this started from (#479's field report, int4; bytes_per_voxel from #324, job 282172105da1), so no projection drops; the #479 points were H3 int4 runs, not this adapter, and no longer bound gb_per_reference

variables.prompt: References: @Image1 is the subject, an astronaut in a white hard-shell suit with a gold-mirrored visor and an orange chest harness. @Audio1 is the voice timbre reference only: a measured, formal male voice, mid-range in pitch. Make a new video of the astronaut from @Image1 speaking directly to camera, head and shoulders, keeping the suit, visor and harness exactly as in @Image1. The astronaut says, in the voice of @Audio1: "We came in peace, and we will leave the light on." SOUND: a soft suit-radio hiss under the voice, faint air-recycler hum. No subtitles, no captions, no text.
variables.subject: https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/diffusers/astronaut.jpg

num_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and Pika H3 Flex generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps (120..360 frames, snapped up onto the 17 * n + 5 grid)

width.reason: Pika H3 Flex's canvas is a multiple of 32 on both axes, and MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses one that is not only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for

height.reason: Pika H3 Flex's canvas is a multiple of 32 on both axes, and MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses one that is not only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
